title: Diphtheria: prevented by antitoxin IgG against the exotoxin
vignette: An 8-year-old boy who recently moved to the United States from Indonesia is brought to the emergency department due to fever, sore throat, and difficulty breathing. His immunization status cannot be determined. Physical examination shows extensive, coalescing, gray pharyngeal exudate and cervical adenopathy. Several days after being admitted to the hospital, he dies of myocarditis and severe heart failure. The presence of which of the following would most likely have prevented this patient's death?

clues.note: Uncertain/incomplete vaccination is the key risk factor for diphtheria, which is vaccine-preventable (DPT/diphtheria toxoid).
A gray, adherent pharyngeal PSEUDOMEMBRANE is the hallmark local lesion of diphtheria (Corynebacterium diphtheriae).

clues.text: dies of myocarditis and severe heart failure
clues.note: Systemic absorption of DIPHTHERIA EXOTOXIN causes myocarditis and neuritis - the lethal complication. Neutralizing antitoxin antibody prevents this.

whatMatters: Unvaccinated child + gray pharyngeal pseudomembrane + fatal myocarditis = DIPHTHERIA. The disease is toxin-mediated; the diphtheria toxoid vaccine generates NEUTRALIZING IgG ANTIBODIES against the circulating EXOTOXIN (the toxin's binding subunit), preventing toxin-mediated cardiac/neural damage. Answer D (IgG against circulating proteins).
strategy: Recognize diphtheria and that death is TOXIN-mediated -> protection requires antibody that NEUTRALIZES the secreted (circulating) exotoxin = IgG antitoxin (from the toxoid vaccine). Reject CD8 T cells (kill virus-infected/tumor cells, not circulating toxin), complement-fixing IgM / T-cell-independent IgM (for encapsulated bacteria; long-term protection is IgG), and IgA against capsular proteins (C. diphtheriae has no polysaccharide capsule, and mucosal IgA doesn't neutralize systemic toxin).

eliminations.label: Activated CD8 T lymphocytes - kill infected/tumor cells, not toxin
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: cytotoxic T cells that destroy virally infected or malignant cells. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they do not bind or neutralize a secreted, circulating bacterial exotoxin. ✅ Correct if: intracellular viral infection or tumor immunity.

eliminations.label: Complement-fixing IgM - extracellular bacteria, not toxin neutralization
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: IgM that fixes complement to opsonize/lyse extracellular bacteria. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: protection here requires NEUTRALIZING antitoxin (IgG), and long-term vaccine immunity is IgG-mediated, not IgM. ✅ Correct if: acute response to an encapsulated bacterium (complement-mediated).

eliminations.label: IgA against capsular proteins - no capsule; wrong compartment
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: mucosal IgA against a polysaccharide capsule. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: C. diphtheriae has NO polysaccharide capsule, and mucosal IgA does not neutralize a toxin absorbed into the bloodstream. ✅ Correct if: mucosal defense against an encapsulated organism (e.g., IgA vs colonization).

eliminations.label: IgM from T-cell-independent response - short-lived, no memory
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: IgM generated against polysaccharide antigens without T-cell help (no class switching/memory). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: durable protective immunity against the diphtheria PROTEIN toxoid is T-cell-dependent IgG, not T-independent IgM. ✅ Correct if: response to a pure polysaccharide antigen.

reasoning: Unvaccinated child + gray pharyngeal pseudomembrane + fatal myocarditis = diphtheria
Death is caused by the systemically absorbed diphtheria EXOTOXIN (ADP-ribosylates EF-2)
Protection requires neutralizing antibody against the secreted (circulating) toxin
The diphtheria toxoid vaccine generates IgG antitoxin -> IgG against circulating proteins; answer D
mechanism: Toxigenic strains of Corynebacterium diphtheriae colonize the pharynx and secrete DIPHTHERIA TOXIN, an exotoxin that ADP-ribosylates elongation factor-2 (EF-2), halting host protein synthesis and killing cells. Local effects include a gray pharyngeal PSEUDOMEMBRANE and cervical lymphadenopathy; systemic absorption of the toxin causes potentially fatal MYOCARDITIS and neuritis. Immunity is TOXIN-directed: the diphtheria toxoid vaccine (part of DPT) induces NEUTRALIZING IgG ANTIBODIES against the toxin's binding (B) subunit, blocking the toxin from entering cells and thereby preventing toxin-mediated damage (it also reduces toxigenic carriage in the population). Because the target is a secreted (circulating) protein, the protective response is IgG ANTITOXIN, not cellular immunity or mucosal/capsular antibodies. The distractors correspond to other defenses: CD8 T cells (intracellular pathogens/tumors), complement-fixing/T-independent IgM (encapsulated bacteria), and IgA against capsules (which C. diphtheriae lacks).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro > diphtheria: toxigenic C. diphtheriae exotoxin ADP-ribosylates EF-2 -> pseudomembrane + myocarditis/neuritis; toxoid vaccine -> neutralizing IgG antitoxin; treat antitoxin + antibiotics.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Toxin-mediated death is prevented by neutralizing IgG against the circulating exotoxin (from toxoid).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on exotoxin/toxoid, antitoxin, ADP-ribosylation of EF-2, pseudomembrane, or neutralizing antibody? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: CD8 T cells (infected/tumor cells), complement IgM / T-independent IgM (encapsulated bacteria), IgA/capsule (no capsule) don't neutralize systemic toxin.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: diphtheria prevented by toxoid -> neutralizing IgG antitoxin; toxin ADP-ribosylates EF-2 -> myocarditis.

keywords.back: Neutralizing IgG antitoxin (from diphtheria toxoid vaccine)
ADP-ribosylates elongation factor-2 (EF-2) -> stops protein synthesis
Inactivated toxin -> antibodies neutralize the real exotoxin

memoryHook: Diphtheria kills with a toxin, so you fight it with an anti-toxin: toxoid vaccine trains IgG to grab the circulating poison before it wrecks the heart.
